title: Percentages and Compound Interest (KS4)
subject: Maths
strapline: Multipliers, increase/decrease, and interest that builds on itself.
facts: A percentage is a number out of 100; to find 30% of an amount, multiply by 0.30.
A multiplier increases or decreases in one step: +15% is ×1.15; −15% is ×0.85.
To find a percentage change: (change ÷ original) × 100.
Simple interest is the same amount each year, based only on the original amount.
Compound interest is added to the total each year, so the next year’s interest is bigger.
Compound growth formula: final amount = start × (multiplier)^number of years.

quick_quiz.q: What single multiplier increases an amount by 20%?
What multiplier decreases an amount by 8%?
Is compound interest more or less than simple interest over time?

teacher_tips: Teach the multiplier method — it scales to compound problems cleanly.
Contrast simple vs compound with a table for the same rate.
Insist on the "×" power for compound rather than repeated addition.
